agree.reason: Dana gets a specific, short, relevant pitch tied to her own $600K figure, but it never turns that figure into savings against cost, so it gives her little reason to push past her IT director.

honest.reason: It credits the halving to one named customer, and 4.1 to 1.9 really is more than half, so it avoids the brief's broader 'we cut errors in half' claim; it does leave out the weaker 2.8 to 2.2 result.

works_the_facts.reason: It doesn't work out the obvious numbers: halving $600K saves about $300K a year, and five sites cost about $75K a year (5 × $1,250 × 12), a roughly 4:1 return the reader never sees.

right_comparison.reason: The alternative of doing nothing, about $600K a year in returns that keeps coming, is only hinted at by the subject line and is never set against the price.

qualification.reason: 'Whether those numbers could hold up in your warehouses' is a fair hedge, but it names no pilot, no date, no target rate and nothing that happens if the target is missed.

objections.reason: 'Sits on top of it, doesn't replace' meets the IT director's main objection, but the email doesn't say how little his team has to touch or integrate, which is what he will ask.

fit.reason: It's short and readable on a phone, with a clear subject line and one call to action, as the brief asked.
